newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bond yields up on higher cost of funding.
newsitem.headline: Greek bond yields up on higher cost of funding.

text.p: Yields of Greek fixed coupon bonds jumped five basis points on selling pressure related to the rising cost of financing around mid-session, dealers said.

"Yields on three-, five- and seven-year fixed coupon bonds have risen five basis points and discount margins on FRNs have also firmed to 50 basis points from 45 basis points," said a bond dealer at a private bank.
The dealer attributed the drop in coupon bond prices to their increased cost of carry.
Dealers said a private bank was looking to unload a good chunk of fixed coupon bonds.
Short-term interbank depos rose 30 to 40 basis points in earlier trade, a fourth of a point in tenors up to three-months and a tenth of a point in six-month to one-year periods, dealers said.
Dealers attributed the pick up in interest rates to tighter liquidity conditions.
Forex forwards were also firmer in line with depos but the long-end of the curve dipped around 1230 local (0930 GMT).
"Depos and forwards are dancing together," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "They are both up since this morning although long forwards are showing some softness now."
The dealer said the market was going to monitor developments at the central bank's fixing for possible liquidity clues.
The drachma was weaker against the ecu trading around 311.15/20, dealers said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
